_doc: USER-BACKEND-1 as data (Rowan, 2026-11-17). Two rules, one check: `python3 -m foundation userbackend --check` (a step in checks.yml). Rule 1, the user/system boundary: the user does their idea and their front end; the system does everything behind it (errors, credentials, deploys, identity linking, retries). Backend work is fully auditable in the owner-only provenance and audit log and never burdens or leaks to the user: no raw backend error text in a user-facing response (the two patterns below match a response or page that carries a caught error; internal records for loops and ledgers are not user-facing and stay raw for the audit). Rule 2, one improvement improves every system: a fix learned anywhere lives in one shared module that every Worker (site, dashboard, tenants, spinoffs, tick, and every tenant built from the seed) imports; a fork fails the check. Consumers: foundation/userbackend.py, tests/foundation/test_userbackend.py, seed/worker/test/errors.test.js. Seed copy: seed/doctrine/user-backend.json.
leak_ok_marker: USER-BACKEND-OK: <reason>  (on the same line; only for a response that never reaches a user, such as an owner-only panel or a service-binding call)

fork_patterns: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS owner_oauth_app

service_binding_exempt.deploy/agents-worker.js: reached only through the tick's service binding; no user-facing route
